title: Pages with `color-scheme: dark` have too low link color contrast

labels.name: a11y-needs-resolution
labels.description: Issue the Accessibility Group has raised and looks for a response on.

body: Now that the standardized [``](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/4504) and the corresponding CSS property [`color-scheme`](https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/3299) have landed in Chrome and Safari, an accessibility issue around link colors occurs: The colors defined in [§14.3.4 Phrasing content](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#phrasing-content-3)… ```css :link { color: #0000EE; } :visited { color: #551A8B; } :link:active, :visited:active { color: #FF0000; } :link, :visited { text-decoration: underline; cursor: pointer; } ``` …do not have sufficient contrast on a dark background. See this [demo](https://color-scheme-demo.glitch.me/) (note the [[Top]](#) links): This issue should probably also affect the definition of the [CSS System Colors](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#typedef-system-color): - *`LinkText`* ([contrast insufficient](https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/?fcolor=0000EE&bcolor=000000)): Text in non-active, non-visited links. - *`VisitedText`* ([contrast insufficient](https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/?fcolor=551B8B&bcolor=000000)): Text in visited links. - *`ActiveText`* ([contrast OK-ish](https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/?fcolor=ff0000&bcolor=000000)): Text in active links. I have also opened bugs for [Chrome](https://crbug.com/1066811), [WebKit](https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=209851), and [Firefox](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1626560) for awareness and to get this fixed.
